owner: feature/r012-server (backend, both portals). The web and Android streams build against this file and copy nothing from it into code by hand: they read routes, fields and limits from here.
enforcedBy: backend/tests/test_data_explorer_contract.py (shared): every route below is mounted in this portal with its method, and the limits and type tokens equal the server's. This file, the shared backend package backend/app/services/data_explorer and backend/app/api/routes/data_explorer.py are byte-identical in both repos through shared/transcription.sha256 (scripts/sync_transcription.py).
compatibility: Every change is additive. A 0.0.11 client that sends none of the new parameters gets exactly the 0.0.11 response shape, plus extra fields it ignores. New clients opt in with slim=1 and the new routes.

featureIds.note: Parity registry ids for shared/questionnaire-features.json. Tag web tests '@qf:<id>' and Android tests '@QFeature("<id>")'. The registry rows are added once all four clients carry their markers (unifiedRelease is true, so a 'planned' row fails CI).
featureIds.X1: Explorer layout: tree first, search as the tree toolbar, all downloads in one place
featureIds.X2: Download size before download: file count and bytes in total and per type (W3, D3)
featureIds.X3: Multi-select folders and files, downloaded together (W11)
featureIds.X4: Thumbnails instead of originals in folder listings (W14)
featureIds.X5: Video, audio, image and PDF preview in a dialog (W12)
featureIds.X6: Table search across every row on the server, and CSV per sheet (W13)
featureIds.X7: Transcript: all formats in one zip, per transcript and per folder
featureIds.X8: Browse by type: pages and a cut notice (W5)
featureIds.X10: Streaming download with progress in bytes, Cancel, failed-file list and resume (W1, W2, W4, D1, D10)
featureIds.X11: Audio to mp4 with a visible fallback to the original under its real name (A10, D2)
featureIds.X12: Open a single transcript on demand instead of from the folder listing (A3)

types.typeToken: images | videos | audios | documents | other | transcripts | text

TreeEntry.name: string
TreeEntry.mediaType: IMAGE | VIDEO | AUDIO | PDF | DOCUMENT | OTHER | absent
TreeEntry.url: string | null (stored object URL; prefer previewPath/downloadPath)
TreeEntry.content: string: text files (details.txt, answers.txt, notes.txt) always; transcript files only when slim is not set
TreeEntry.transcriptPath: string: GET path of this file's transcript text (A3). Present on transcript files and on media whose transcriptAvailable is true
TreeEntry.thumbnailPath: string: present on IMAGE media. GET it with ?size=256|512 (W14)
TreeEntry.previewPath: string: present on IMAGE, VIDEO, AUDIO and PDF media (W12)
TreeEntry.downloadPath: string: GET path of the file itself

Stats.bytes: int (bytes of media whose size is known; text and transcripts count their UTF-8 length)
Stats.truncated: bool (the walk hit manifestMaxFiles or the depth cap)

ManifestFile.originalPath: string | absent: the name to save under when the response says X-Conversion: original

query.slim: 1 to leave transcript text out of entries (A3). New clients always send it.
query.cursor: string | absent: the nextCursor of the previous page
query.status: FR only: review status filter for the tree, unchanged

routes.response: {path, crumbs, entries: [TreeEntry], info, truncated: bool, total: int, nextCursor: string | null, taxonomies, taxonomy, designWorkshopsVisible (DR), designWorkshopsDownloadable (DR)}
routes.notes: Removed recordings (removedAt set) never appear (A1). 0.0.14: every source list is read to its end in batches of treeTake (keyset on id after its own order), so a level holds every entry, total is the true count and truncated is always false; nextCursor pages the entries of this level in their shown order, treePageMax at a time. 0.0.13: every file entry carries capturedAt (ISO; the recording's recordedAt, else createdAt; null for text entries). Every folder entry carries count and bytes: the stored files (photos, videos, recordings, documents; not transcripts or details text) under it, from one grouped query per listing. They are numbers on every by-workshop level (workshops, crafts, artisans, an artisan's products, tools and questionnaire, a product's processes, a process's steps, sittings, tools), every by-design-workshop level, by-type and every by-uploader level, and null only on the repository root, the legacy users levels and the transcripts folders. by-workshop and by-design-workshop are computed set-based from the same reach rules as the walk (backend/app/services/data_explorer/reach.py), with a constant number of statements per listing.

routes.response: {mediaId, name, content: string, language: string | null}
routes.notes: One transcript, fetched when the user opens it (A3). 404 for a removed or unreadable recording. Clients cache it for the session; never fetch twice for one open (W16).
What a download of this folder would contain, before downloading (W3, D3). Same walk as the manifest, without the file list.

Android folder downloads include everything by default (owner decision 3): send no include. Every line carries sizeBytes and sha256 (hex, null when unknown; for a convertToMp4 line sha256 is null and originalSha256 describes the stored original). A client skips a file it already has with that digest and size, and Range-resumes the original through /data/media/{media_id}/download?format=original, which redirects to storage that honours Range. The converted .mp4 stream does not. Every line also carries capturedAt (null for text).

routes.body: {paths: [string] (<= manifestMaxPaths), mediaIds: [string] (<= manifestMaxMediaIds), include: [typeToken] | null, stream: bool}
routes.notes: Multi-select download (W11). Each selected folder becomes a top-level folder named as in the tree (made unique); selected files sit at the top level. A media file selected twice appears once. Every line carries sizeBytes and sha256 (hex, null when unknown; for a convertToMp4 line sha256 is null and originalSha256 describes the stored original). A client skips a file it already has with that digest and size, and Range-resumes the original through /data/media/{media_id}/download?format=original, which redirects to storage that honours Range. The converted .mp4 stream does not. Every line also carries capturedAt (null for text).

routes.response: 302 to a signed WebP URL (generated once and kept in storage); Cache-Control: private, max-age=1800. 404 when the media is not an image, 415 when it cannot be decoded: show the type icon.
routes.notes: Never load the original in a listing (W14).

routes.response: 302 to a signed inline URL (Content-Disposition: inline, Range supported by storage); Cache-Control: private, max-age=1800.
routes.notes: Video, audio, image and PDF (W12). 415 for other types.

query.variant: original | isolated, default original; isolated signs the clear-voices copy, 404 when there is none

query.format: mp4 | original | absent. Absent means mp4 for audio (as in 0.0.11) and the original for everything else
query.fallback: original: if conversion fails, stream the original instead of an error (D2)

headers.Content-Disposition: the name to save under: the .mp4 name when converted, the real name when original
headers.Content-Length: set for originals; absent for a streamed conversion

routes.notes: Conversion streams through ffmpeg, copies AAC audio without re-encoding, runs one at a time per server, and counts failures (A10). If ffmpeg fails after the first bytes the connection is cut, so a client never keeps a half file: retry, then ask with fallback=original. An original is a 307 to a signed URL that is reused for signedUrlReuseSeconds (A13), so a repeat play or download is a cache hit; resume with Range against that URL (D1, D10). Removed recordings are 404.

query.sheet: sheet name: required for csv, optional for json (only that sheet is returned)
query.q: string: json only. Rows of every sheet (or of sheet) that contain every word, case-insensitive, searched across all rows on the server (W13)
query.offset: int >= 0, default 0, json only: skip this many rows (or matched rows when q) and return the next reportPreviewRows (reportSearchMaxRows when q). Additive: absent is the first page. Page with sheet=<name> and offset += rows returned until rows run out or the next offset reaches totalRows (matchedRows when q). Each json sheet echoes offset.
query.sheets: comma-separated sheet names | absent: every sheet (xlsx)
query.rows: all | filtered, default all; filtered keeps the rows matching q, with no preview cap (xlsx)
query.links: 1 | 0, default 1; 0 drops the URL and Media URLs columns (xlsx)
query.name: file name without a path; sanitised to ASCII and given .xlsx (xlsx)

routes.response: json: {sheets: [{name, color, columns, rows, truncated, preview, capped, totalRows, matchedRows (when q)}], previewRows, query}. csv: the one sheet, UTF-8 with BOM, streamed. xlsx: unchanged. A sheet the viewer may not download is not offered as csv. Every json sheet carries rowNumbers: int[] parallel to rows, the 1-based place of each row in the whole sheet (preview 1..n, search the matched rows' own places); a cap note row is numbered 0 and comes only on the first page and the last page.
routes.notes: Requests queue, one build at a time; 503 with Retry-After: 15 only when 8 are waiting or one waited 90 s. One build per folder and data version is cached and serves the preview, every q search, the csv and the xlsx. json adds builtAt and cached. In the json preview a transcript cell is cut to reportPreviewTranscriptChars; the xlsx and csv stay complete (A6). Errors are always JSON with a 4xx/5xx status: check the status and the PK signature before saving, and never Range-resume a report.

routes.response: format=zip: one zip holding every format of that transcript (md and docx with and without timestamps, srt and vtt for each track that has timing). track and timestamps are ignored for zip.

A streamed zip of every transcript in that folder and below, each in every format the transcript has (md and docx with and without timestamps, srt and vtt per track), in the folder layout of the tree. Content-Disposition carries the name.
routes.notes: Per-folder 'all formats in one zip' (owner decision 6). Streamed; nothing is held whole in memory.
Fills the transcript language filter (W8). Counts only what this user may read.

query.type: artisan | product | tool | workshop | craft | interview | process | media
query.q: string: case-insensitive, matched on the server across every row, not only the current page (W5, W16)

routes.response: {type, items: [{id, name, creator: string | null, createdAt: string | null}], total, page, pageSize, pages, truncated: bool}
routes.notes: Browse by type (W5). Newest first. Removed recordings never appear (A1). FR includes every review status (owner decision 1, W6 dropped). truncated is true when total > page * pageSize: show 'Showing N of TOTAL' and offer the next page.

routes.response: {items: [TreeEntry (kind file)], total, page, pageSize, pages, truncated: bool}
routes.notes: The files of one record picked in Browse by type, with thumbnailPath, previewPath and downloadPath like the tree.
Clients read it once per screen and at most every 10 minutes, and update it locally after a dictation.
ReportOptions = {sheets: string[] | null, answers: original | english | both, rows: all | filtered, links: bool}. Per user.
Remember these choices. 422 for an unknown value.

query.offset: int >= 0, default 0: skip this many of the folder's recordings. Additive: absent is the first page

routes.response: {items: [{mediaId, name, path, mediaType: AUDIO | VIDEO, hasText, capturedAt, snippet?}], total, truncated, query, offset, nextOffset: int | null}
routes.notes: The Transcripts tab. snippet only when q is given. Each page walks transcriptListMax recordings of the folder (q filters within them); ask again with offset=nextOffset until it is null to reach the last recording.

routes.response: one .docx with every readable transcript under the folder, in the transcripts-list order
routes.notes: Runs through the report queue (503 with Retry-After when full). 404 when the folder has no readable transcript.

routes.response: {peaks: number[] (800 values, 0..1), durationMs: int | null, isolated: bool, canIsolate: bool}
routes.notes: Computed once with ffmpeg and stored. 404 when the file is not audio or video or cannot be decoded; 503 with Retry-After while another waveform is being made. isolated: a clear-voices copy exists (play it from preview?variant=isolated). canIsolate: POST isolate would be accepted (audio, no copy yet, the admin switch on and keyed, the caller uploaded it or is a content admin, consent allows).

routes.response: {path, visitedAt, previousVisitAt: string | null, newFiles: int, newTranscripts: int}
routes.notes: Records this visit and counts what arrived under the folder since the previous one (0 on a first visit). 404 for a folder the caller cannot see.

routes.response: {path, title, subtitle, totals: {files, bytes, fields: {filled, total}, transcripts: {total, ready, translating, failed}, review: {approved, pending, total}}, sections: [{key, label}], artisans: [{id, name, craft, path, fields, media: {files, bytes}, transcripts, review, sections: [{key, state: complete | partial | missing, missing: string[], href: string | null}]}], truncated}
routes.notes: Workshop coverage. 404 for a path that is not a workshop folder. The client sorts. href opens that section of the artisan's sitting that answered it (else the latest sitting): /questionnaire/sessions/<interviewId>/view?section=<code>; null when the artisan has no sitting.
View = {id, name, path, state: {view: files | tables | transcripts, sheet, q, filters}, shared, mine, ownerName, createdAt, updatedAt}. shared lists only views whose folder the caller can see.
The owner, or anyone who can see the folder of a shared view; otherwise 404. Web link: /data?viewId=<id>.
Owner only.
Owner only.
Queues the existing audio-isolation job for one recording. 403 when canIsolate is false, 404 when the file is not visible or not audio.

routes.response: {items: Schedule[], enabled, mailAvailable, maxPerOwner, attachMaxBytes, defaultTimezone}
routes.notes: The caller's own scheduled reports. Schedule = {id, savedViewId, viewName, path, weekday (0 Monday..6 Sunday), hourLocal (0..23), timezone, label, options, paused, nextRunAt, lastSentAt, lastError, lastFile: {fileName, sizeBytes, attached} | null, createdAt}.
Any saved view the caller may open (their own, or shared with a visible folder); else 404. Defaults Monday 08:00 Asia/Kolkata. The first e-mail goes at the next occurrence.
Owner only. Resuming never sends a missed week at once.
Owner only.
The last workbook sent, as a 15-minute signed link. Owner only, and only while the owner can still see the folder; else 404. Web page: /data/report-schedules/<id>.
No sign-in: the e-mailed token is the credential. 404 for an unknown token. Web page: /report-schedule/unsubscribe?token=<token>.
No sign-in. Pauses the schedule the token names; the owner can resume it in Saved views.

clientRules: Removed recordings are already left out by the server everywhere (A1); clients never filter them.
Stream zips to disk with a zip64 writer; never hold an archive in memory (W1).
Fetch suggestedParallelFetches files at a time and suggestedParallelConversions conversions (W1).
On X-Conversion: original save under originalPath, never under the .mp4 name (D2).
A file that fails 3 times is left out of the zip and listed (D1, W4).

sorting.param: sort=<key>:<dir>, dir asc | desc. Absent means the list's default, which is the order the list had before 0.0.15. A key the route does not allow, or a malformed value, answers 422.

meaning.name: the shown name, case-folded
meaning.recorded: files: recordedAt, else createdAt. Folders: the record's own date (a workshop's startDate, else its date; other records recordedAt, else createdAt). Search: the index recordDate
meaning.added: createdAt of the file or the folder's record
meaning.modified: updatedAt of the file or the folder's record
meaning.duration: audio and video: the current transcript version's durationMs, else the waveform's durationMs
meaning.type: files: mediaType (text files read TEXT). Folders: recordType

sorting.response: tree, transcripts-list, browse, browse-media and search-unified answer sort: {key, dir} (what was applied) and sorts: [key] (the keys that mean something for this list, in menu order). A client shows only those keys and falls back to the default when a remembered key is not among them.
sorting.order: The server sorts the whole list before it pages it, so every page continues the same order. Folders stay before files. A missing value sorts last in either direction. Ties break by name (case-folded), then by id (mediaId, else path).
sorting.availability: name always; recorded, added and modified when an entry carries that date; size when an entry has a size; duration when the list holds audio or video; type when more than one type is listed; workshop, artisan, craft and status only in mixed lists, when the files span more than one of them.
sorting.memory: Remembered per viewer per list level, on the device: web localStorage dataExplorer.sort.<viewer>.<level>, Android the explorer preferences under the same name. Levels: tree:<first path segment or root>:<depth>, transcripts, browse:<type>, browse-media:<type>, search:<type or all>.
sorting.peer: Cross-portal search forwards sort in the POST /search body; each portal sorts its own page and the merge interleaves by the same key, ties local first.
